clue.text: Reach route through mountains — result!

definitions.note: used as a verb: to result is to happen as a consequence

parts.note: to reach a total or state is to come to it
a pass is a gap or road through a mountain range

explanation.surface: A traveller finally reaches the mountain pass they were aiming for and celebrates.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb phrase meaning to happen or come about, as an outcome does.

clue.text: Bird found in pile of hay

definitions.meaning: a haycock is a conical heap of hay in a field, shortened here

explanation.surface: A bird nesting in a haystack.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a male chicken and a small conical stack of hay left to dry.

clue.text: Tie up North African

definitions.meaning: to tie up a boat is to secure it at a ...
a member of the Muslim people of north-west Africa, historically in Spain

explanation.surface: An instruction to bind up someone from North Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to secure a vessel; the noun is the historic name for a Berber or Arab of the Maghreb.

clue.text: Leader of excavation in ancient city, keen to break out spades as just what's needed

indicators.note: the excavation's leader is placed within the ancient city's name

parts.note: Thebes was a great city of ancient Egypt (and of Greece)

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
breaking out suggests the letters of keen bursting into a new arrangement

parts.note: S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: An archaeologist leading a dig in an ancient city is keen to start digging with spades.
explanation.walkthrough: Thebes was a great city of ancient Egypt; 'to break out' rearranges the four letters of 'keen' into a joint of the leg.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal idiom for something excellent, exactly the thing wanted.

clue.text: China leased equipment used in warehouse

parts.note: Cockney rhyming slang: china plate = mate, so china means pal
let means rented out, as a leased property is

explanation.surface: A Chinese firm leased storage gear to a warehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: China here is rhyming slang for a friend, not the country: 'china plate' rhymes with 'mate'.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat wooden platform on which goods are stacked and moved by forklift in storage depots.

clue.text: Birds make disturbance in yards

indicators.note: the commotion word is set inside the word for yards

parts.note: on a sailing ship the yards are spars holding the sails
a row is a noisy quarrel or commotion

explanation.surface: Birds kick up a racket in people's back gardens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yards' suggests gardens, but here it means the spars of a ship's rigging.
explanation.definitionFit: Small brown songbirds, common in towns, are examples of birds.

clue.text: Eats fast food item around one third off

definitions.note: informal plural noun for food, matched by a slang mass noun

indicators.note: turned around, so the shortened word is read backwards
two of the six letters, a third of the word, are removed from the end

parts.note: a burger is a staple of fast-food outlets

explanation.surface: Someone wolfs down a burger in a few bites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one third off' drops ER from BURGER to leave BURG, which 'around' turns back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang for food in general, so one informal word replaces the other.

clue.text: Frightful horn is core to identify this animal

indicators.note: the letters are put into a frightful mess, a new order

explanation.surface: A scary horn at the centre of its face lets you name this beast.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface itself points to the horned animal, so the whole clue is a nudge as well as an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The large thick-skinned mammal with a nose horn, as the surface describes.

clue.text: Rail links globe endlessly with American business

indicators.note: without its end, the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a globe is a sphere, a ball
US, the United States
trade means commerce, business

explanation.surface: A rail network connects the world, without limit, to American commerce.
explanation.definitionFit: A row of small pillars topped by a handrail, as on a staircase or balcony.

clue.text: Lucky shape: clubs logo's origin on next page

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: a word's origin is its first letter

parts.note: overleaf means on the other side of the page

explanation.surface: A club's lucky emblem, where the logo began, appears on the following page.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-leaf one is a traditional good-luck symbol; also the shape of a road junction.

clue.text: Clinton's draft law

definitions.meaning: the first name of US President Clinton, with 's as 'Clinton is'
a proposed law before Parliament or Congress

explanation.surface: A piece of legislation drafted by President Clinton.
explanation.definitionFit: The forename of the 42nd US president, and the term for a proposed piece of legislation.

clue.text: Sort of power my generation endlessly put out without carbon

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside: the rearranged letters surround the carbon
put out of order, so the letters are rearranged
without its end, the final letter of the phrase is dropped

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A singer laments how their generation keeps emitting, minus carbon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops N from MY GENERATION; 'put out' rearranges the rest to ATOMIENERGY, which 'without' (meaning outside) wraps round C.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclear power is a kind of power derived from splitting atoms.

clue.text: Cooked a nice lobster for special occasions

indicators.note: cooked as in cooked up, the letters reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A lovely lobster prepared for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Parties and festivities held to mark special events.

clue.text: Handy place where nuns stay around eastern Ulster

indicators.note: the nuns' house is placed around the other letters

parts.note: a convent is a community house for nuns
E is the standard abbreviation for east or eastern
NI, Northern Ireland, often called Ulster

explanation.surface: A useful convent somewhere in the east of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Something conveniently placed or easy to use is handy.

clue.text: Do like everyone else and take interest in court case

parts.note: to follow something, such as a team or news story, is to take an interest in it
a suit is a lawsuit, a case brought in court

explanation.surface: Someone joins the crowd by taking an interest in a trial.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom from card games for doing the same thing as others.

clue.text: Person playing is taken in by android that won't start

indicators.note: the word is is held inside the shortened android
a word that won't start has lost its first letter

parts.note: an android is a humanlike robot

explanation.surface: A musician is fooled by a robot that refuses to switch on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Person playing' looks like part of the surface story; it is a whole definition, a musician who plays a particular reed instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A musician who plays the oboe is one kind of person playing an instrument.

clue.text: Women I am with get very hot outside in beach clothes

indicators.note: the scorching word goes around the other letters

parts.note: to sear is to scorch or burn
I'm, the contraction of I am

explanation.surface: Women and I get sunburnt while wearing our beach outfits.
explanation.definitionFit: Costumes and trunks are the clothes worn for bathing at the seaside.

clue.text: Special equipment for police in South American city with great rampaging

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro in Brazil, usually just Rio

indicators.note: the letters run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Police kit for handling great crowds rampaging in Rio.
explanation.definitionFit: Helmets, shields and armour issued to police for controlling disorder.

clue.text: Depression shown by North American spies in Spanish city

parts.note: a vale is a valley, a depression in land
the CIA, the US Central Intelligence Agency

explanation.surface: Low spirits among US agents stationed in a Spanish city.
explanation.definitionFit: The third-largest city in Spain, on the east coast.

clue.text: Agreement with current line

parts.note: AC, alternating current
a cord is a thin rope or line

explanation.surface: An agreement made along current lines.
explanation.definitionFit: An accord is a formal agreement or harmony between parties.

clue.text: Criticism made by one politician over international body holding good

definitions.note: a noun phrase standing for the verb: criticism made, i.e. to criticise

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
MP, Member of Parliament

indicators.note: the international body holds the letter for good

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations

explanation.surface: An MP's criticism of the United Nations for its good work.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer is a verb, to challenge or criticise, so 'Criticism made' must be read as making criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: To call something into question is to criticise or challenge it.

clue.text: Man sent tweet spinning religious writing

indicators.note: spinning letters land in a new order

explanation.surface: A man sends a tweet that goes viral.
explanation.definitionFit: The Christian scriptures from the Gospels to Revelation, the second part of the Bible.

clue.text: Member of clergy losing head in a short time

indicators.note: the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a canon is a member of a cathedral chapter

explanation.surface: A cleric is quickly beheaded.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned word for soon, shortly.

clue.text: Look up and down

indicators.note: in a down entry the word reads the same going up as going down

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: An instruction to scan someone from head to toe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look up and down' suggests an inspection, but the answer simply reads the same either way in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick glance is a brief look.

clue.text: For seamstress it's the case in perpetuity

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: Something holds true forever for a dressmaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's the case' poses as 'it is true'; it actually means a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A small ornamental container for needles and pins, a sewing case.

clue.text: Another case concerning money running short before end of voyage

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: the final letter is dropped

parts.note: currency is money in circulation

indicators.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Another instance of money running out before the trip is over.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeat occurrence is one more instance of something happening.

clue.text: Pretentious rubbish displayed by English gallery

parts.note: tat is cheap tasteless goods, showy junk

explanation.surface: An English gallery is showing pretentious junk.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is the group of national art galleries in London and elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's best-known modern-art gallery is a specific example of a gallery.

clue.text: Make bloomer over biscuit

parts.note: a make or brand is a manufacturer's label

indicators.note: turned over, so the flower is read backwards

parts.note: a pansy is a flower, something that blooms

explanation.surface: Commit a blunder involving a biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a mistake (or a loaf), but here it is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin, crisp, rolled ginger biscuit, often filled with cream.
